results.summary: This project implements a finite-state-machine controller for a simplified washing machine in Verilog. It progresses through washing stages when the door is closed and the start button is pressed, with the wash duration selectable via a lever. Outputs drive LEDs and control signals for water valve, wash motor, and spin motor. It is intended as an educational example and requires external LEDs, a debounced button, and two levers for testing.

This is an 8-bit SUBNEG CPU implemented in Verilog that requires external parallel SRAM for program and data storage. It interfaces to the SRAM through an address latch and provides a bidirectional bus for data, with additional outputs for control signals and internal state bits. The program must be preloaded into the SRAM by an external device, and the CPU is enabled via a dedicated pin. External hardware includes 3.3V SRAM, address and output latches, and a device to display the 8-bit output.

This project implements a basic oscilloscope and signal generator on an ASIC using VHDL. It samples an analog input via an external ADC, buffers samples in an external FRAM, and displays the captured waveform on an HDMI screen. A direct digital synthesis signal generator produces sine, square, triangle, and sawtooth waveforms via an external DAC. The design requires multiple Pmods (ADC, DAC, FRAM, HDMI, buttons, switches) and outputs settings via UART; the display is rotated 90 degrees due to memory constraints.

This is a simple game that determines which of eight buttons was pressed first. When a button is pressed, the corresponding output is set high if no other button was pressed earlier, and the output can drive LEDs or a 7-segment display. The design is implemented in Wokwi and requires external buttons and output indicators for testing. It is a minimal demonstration of first-input detection.

This analog project provides a configurable multiplexer using passgates, allowing 4:1 or 8:1 analog signal routing. It includes a ring oscillator and a digital counter to generate control signals, enabling characterization of the passgates and chaining of multiplexers. The design is intended for analog experimentation and debugging, requiring external analog hardware for testing. Documentation is limited to a video and brief description.

This is a Brokaw bandgap voltage reference implemented in SKY130 using PNP BJTs, producing a stable ~1.2V output. It includes a PTAT current generator and an OTA-based summing amplifier for temperature readout. The design is tested by applying 1.8V and measuring the reference voltage across temperature. No external hardware is required.

This project implements a simple I2C master controller that transmits one byte to a fixed slave address (0x50). It generates START and STOP conditions and provides BUSY, DONE, and ACK status outputs. The controller is used by asserting START and placing data on the inputs, then observing SCL and SDA activity. External hardware such as an I2C slave, logic analyzer, or oscilloscope is needed for testing.

This project wraps a high-speed crystal oscillator IP block from Chipalooza 2024 into the Tiny Tapeout analog template. It requires an external passive crystal, load capacitors, and a bias current source to operate as a Pierce oscillator. When enabled, it produces a clock signal on a digital output after a start-up delay. The design supports crystals between 4 and 16 MHz, though higher frequencies may need shorter traces.

This project reads up to six external photodiodes as digital inputs and displays the sum on a 7-segment display. It can be tested using dip switches instead of photodiodes, with one switch selecting step or continuous sampling mode. The design is implemented in Wokwi and requires external hardware such as a breadboard, resistors, and photodiodes. It serves as a simple light intensity sensor demonstration.

This project implements a 52-entry 6-bit FIFO using a chain of latches for the first 48 entries and a ring of flip-flops for the last four. It supports write, pop, and peek operations, with a ready signal indicating when the latch chain can accept new data. The design has minimal read-side delays but can refuse writes when the chain is not ready, even if not completely full. It is tested by writing data, popping entries, and observing outputs.
